item.content:encoded:
Laboratory Results & Trends

This section contains laboratory test results with interactive charts showing trends over time.

Lab Types

Chemistry Panel

  • Electrolytes (sodium, potassium, chloride, CO2)
  • Kidney function (creatinine, BUN)
  • Liver function (bilirubin, AST, ALT, albumin, ALP)
  • Blood glucose
  • Calcium, magnesium, phosphate

Hematology

  • CBC (Complete Blood Count)
  • WBC (white blood cells) and differential
  • RBC (red blood cells)
  • Hemoglobin and hematocrit
  • Platelets
  • PT/INR and PTT

Tumor Markers

  • CEA (Carcinoembryonic antigen) — Primary marker for colorectal cancer
  • CA 19-9 — GI malignancy marker

Coagulation Studies

  • PT (prothrombin time)
  • INR (International normalized ratio)
  • PTT (Partial thromboplastin time)
  • D-dimer

Charts & Visualization

Laboratory trends are presented with interactive Chart.js visualizations showing:

  • Values over time
  • Reference ranges (normal values)
  • Clinically significant changes
  • Treatment-related patterns

Frequency

Labs are typically obtained:

  • Before each chemotherapy cycle (biweekly) for CBC, CMP
  • Periodic imaging assessment (every 2-3 months) for staging labs
  • As needed for clinical management

Reading Laboratory Results

Key Points:

  • Normal reference ranges vary between laboratories
  • Values are compared to baseline and prior results
  • Trends are often more significant than individual values
  • Clinical context is essential for interpretation

Individual lab result pages are available showing detailed values and charts.
